subject: Re: [Acme] Model evals & regression after v1.10 rollout
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Huang <jessica@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Model evals & regression after v1.10 rollout

Hi Jessica — great call today, thanks for walking through the two primary workflows (customer support summarization + automated triage). Quick recap and recommended next steps so we're all aligned: 

1) Findings from discovery
- Summarization quality is your top acceptance criteria (short summary, accurate intent capture).
- Throughput requirements: ~200 reqs/min sustained, 1.5s 95p latency target.
- You saw a measurable drop in summary freshness/conciseness after last week's platform model update.

2) Our initial recommendations
- Recommended model: rw-compact-1.9 for the summary pipeline (best balance of latency and fidelity for your prompt set).
- If you need lower tail latency for spikes, we can run a short canary on rw-fast-1.10 with KV cache priming.
- Immediate safety net: pin the production route to rw-compact-1.9 while we run targeted evals.

3) Next steps (proposed)
- Marissa (me) to drop the prompt set and an initial benchmark export to this thread (attached: acme_prompt_set_v2.json).
- Priya to run automated evals comparing v1.10 vs v1.9 on the attached prompt set and share a diff report.
- If regression confirmed, we can either roll back to v1.9 or deploy a canary rollback/patch plan; Priya to propose canary plan and expected impact.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up on Monday to review results and procurement/contract implications.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v2.json (prompt set + expected outputs; redwood eval format).

Thanks — let me know if anything is off in the recap.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-1298

--

From: Jessica Huang <jessica@acme.com>

Date: 2026-06-11T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model evals & regression after v1.10 rollout

Thanks, Marissa — that recap is perfect. A couple quick notes from our side after we dug into the samples: 

- We observed a ~7% drop in satisfaction on the summary facet (shortness/precision) starting 2026-06-04 which correlates with your reported v1.10 rollout.
- The issue is most visible on multi-paragraph tickets where the model now tends to over-abstract and drop key actions.

Can you confirm: is there an easy rollback to the prior model version for the production route? Our CS team is escalating and procurement is asking for timelines. We’d prefer a rollback if that’s low-risk. If not, a canary + quick patch would work.

Also looping in procurement (procure@acme.com) to keep them in the loop on any contract/credits discussion.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jessica
Jessica Huang
Head of Customer Experience, Acme Inc
jessica@acme.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jessica Huang <jessica@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model evals & regression after v1.10 rollout

On Fri, Jun 11, 2026 at 9:30 AM Jessica Huang <jessica@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Marissa — that recap is perfect. A couple quick notes from our side after we dug into the samples: 
> 
> - We observed a ~7% drop in satisfaction on the summary facet (shortness/precision) starting 2026-06-04 which correlates with your reported v1.10 rollout.

Hi all — quick technical plan from SE: 

1) Immediate actions (next 24 hours)
- I’ll run a focused eval comparing rw-compact-1.9 (baseline) vs rw-fast-1.10 using acme_prompt_set_v2.json. Expect an automated diff report (per-example delta + aggregate metrics) within 8 hours.
- I’m attaching the initial report templates and the canary rollout plan for your review (attachments: benchmark_report_v1.10_vs_v1.9.pdf, canary_rollout_plan.md).

2) Recommended mitigations
- Low-risk option: pin your production route to rw-compact-1.9 (we can do this today; no infra downtime). This will immediately restore the prior model behavior.
- Canary rollback: deploy rw-compact-1.9 to 10% of traffic for 24 hours, evaluate production signals (latency, summary quality via sampled evals, error rate). If metrics look good, increase to 50% and then flip.
- Prompt-level fix: if regression is limited to a few prompt patterns, we can ship targeted prompt engineering + prompt templates as a faster fix without changing model version.

3) Risk & tradeoffs
- Rolling back pins you to v1.9 which may be slightly higher latency on some tails but is stable for quality.
- Rolling forward and tuning prompts keeps the newer kernels but may need multiple iterations.

Let me know which path you prefer. If Acme wants immediate remediation, I recommend pinning to v1.9 + running canary evals in parallel so we don’t block feature velocity.

Thanks — I’ll upload the diff report as soon as it’s ready.

– Priya
Priya Natarajan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Model evals & regression after v1.10 rollout

Thanks Priya and Jessica — appreciate the quick triage. Proposed plan and asks: 

Action plan (agreed immediate)
- Today: Redwood to pin Acme prod route to rw-compact-1.9 to restore baseline quality (no downtime). Priya to kick off the canary eval in parallel.
- Monday 2026-06-15 10:00 AM PT: 30-min follow-up to review Priya’s diff report and confirm whether to flip permanently or iterate on prompts. Calendar invite to follow.
- Procurement (procure@acme.com): if rollback/pin has billing or SLA impacts we’ll document the time window and propose a small service credit for the regression window; happy to coordinate separately.

Open items
- Priya: please post the per-example diff link to this thread and a short summary slide we can share with Acme execs.
- Marcus: can you validate expected latency delta for rw-compact-1.9 at 200 reqs/min so procurement has the perf numbers?

I’ve attached the prompt set and will add links to the HubSpot deal record and the evaluation run once available.

Thanks — we’ll treat this as high priority and keep you updated every step of the way.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: benchmark_report_v1.10_vs_v1.9.pdf, canary_rollout_plan.md
